name: Romeo and Juliet
kicker: Shakespeare’s doomed young lovers · Feuding Verona families
briefing: Two teenagers from warring families fall in love at first sight at a masked ball, secretly marry the very next day, and are both dead within a week. William Shakespeare’s _Romeo and Juliet_ turns one bloody Verona street brawl into one of the most quoted love stories ever written, giving English its balcony scene, its “wherefore art thou,” and its most famous double tragedy.
answerHtml: Romeo and Juliet (or The Tragedy of Romeo and Juliet)
accept: the tragedy of romeo and juliet
the most excellent and lamentable tragedy of romeo and juliet

qb.tip: All 8 are clean hits on this exact answer line. Real packets almost never name the two lovers directly in the clues, calling them “a character in this play” instead — worth imitating in your own notes.

sample.note: the 8 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: This play opens with a 14-line sonnet spoken by a Chorus, introducing “two households, both alike in dignity.” Later, one witty young man mockingly nicknames a rival swordsman the “Prince of Cats” shortly before being killed by him in a duel.
tossups.r: That same witty young man had earlier delivered a wild speech about the fairy Queen Mab on the way to a masked ball. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare tragedy about two “star-cross’d lovers” from the feuding Montague and Capulet families.

tossups.p: Believing his new bride is dead, the hero of this play buys deadly poison from a poor apothecary in the city of Mantua. He is misled by a servant named Balthasar, who wrongly reports that his secretly-married wife has died.
tossups.r: A friendly friar had secretly married the couple and later given the heroine a sleeping potion to fake her own death. For 10 points, name this tragedy that ends with both young lovers taking their own lives, written by William Shakespeare.

tossups.p: This play’s heroine relies on her talkative old Nurse to carry secret messages to her new husband. Earlier, a street brawl breaks out between the two households’ servants, and the peacemaking Benvolio tries to stop it.
tossups.r: The feuding families are the Montagues and the Capulets. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play in which a wild speech about the fairy Queen Mab is delivered by Mercutio on the way to a masked ball.

tossups.p: The ruler of this play’s setting, Prince Escalus, warns that any more street fighting between its two feuding families will be punished by death. Late in the play, the hero kills Count Paris, his bride’s unwanted arranged fiance, in a duel outside her tomb.
tossups.r: The grieving Montagues and Capulets finally reconcile and agree to raise golden statues in memory of their dead children. For 10 points, name this tragedy set in Verona, written by William Shakespeare.

tossups.p: At the end of a famous nighttime scene, this play’s heroine tells her admirer that “parting is such sweet sorrow.” Earlier in that same balcony scene, she wonders aloud, “what’s in a name?”
tossups.r: The hero first attends the fateful ball hoping to see a different girl, Rosaline, who never actually appears onstage. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare tragedy about two star-crossed lovers from warring Verona households.

tossups.p: A servant named Balthasar wrongly tells this play’s exiled hero that his secret bride has died in Verona. Earlier in the story, that hero’s friend delivers a wild speech about the fairy Queen Mab on the way to a masked ball.
tossups.r: The hothead Tybalt kills that same friend, Mercutio, and is then killed himself, which gets the hero banished. For 10 points, name this tragedy of two doomed lovers from the feuding Montague and Capulet families.

tossups.p: This play’s Prince Escalus threatens death to end the fighting between its two noble households. Its hero first goes to a masked ball hoping to see a girl named Rosaline, who never appears as a character.
tossups.r: He instead falls instantly in love with his host’s daughter, leading to a secret marriage performed by a friendly friar. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare play about star-crossed lovers from the feuding Montague and Capulet families.

tossups.p: This play’s heroine wonders aloud “what’s in a name?” during a famous scene on her balcony. A friar in this play secretly marries the two young lovers and later gives the heroine a sleeping potion.
tossups.r: That potion is meant to help her fake her own death and escape a marriage to Count Paris. For 10 points, name this tragedy that ends with both lovers truly dying, written by William Shakespeare.

tossups.p: This play opens with a street brawl between two households’ servants that the even-tempered Benvolio tries to break up. Its hero later kills the hothead Tybalt in revenge for the death of his witty friend Mercutio.
tossups.r: That revenge killing gets the hero banished from the city of Verona. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare tragedy about a pair of “star-cross’d lovers” from the feuding Montague and Capulet families.

tossups.p: A friendly friar in this play secretly marries its two teenaged leads and later supplies a sleeping potion. Its hero buys real poison from a poor apothecary after wrongly hearing, from the servant Balthasar, that his bride has died.
tossups.r: The grieving families finally reconcile over their children’s graves and agree to raise golden statues in their memory. For 10 points, name this tragedy of two star-crossed lovers, written by William Shakespeare.

tossups.p: This play’s hero attends a masked ball hoping to see a girl named Rosaline, who the audience never actually meets. On the way to that same ball, his friend delivers a comic speech describing the tiny fairy Queen Mab and her hazelnut carriage.
tossups.r: That friend, Mercutio, is later killed by the hothead Tybalt, who is the cousin of the hero’s new secret wife. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare tragedy set among the feuding Montague and Capulet families of Verona.

tossups.p: This play’s Prince Escalus threatens death for any more street brawling between its two feuding noble households. Its hero kills Count Paris, his new wife’s unwanted arranged fiance, during a duel outside her family tomb.
tossups.r: He has come to the tomb because he mistakenly believes, after a servant’s wrong message, that his secret bride has actually died. For 10 points, name this tragedy ending in a real double death, written by William Shakespeare.

tossups.p: This play’s heroine first meets her future husband at a masked ball thrown by her own family. She later leans out over a balcony, not realizing he can hear her, and wonders aloud “what’s in a name?”
tossups.r: Her cousin Tybalt is killed soon after by that same balcony-climbing suitor, sparking his banishment from Verona. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare tragedy about two star-cross’d lovers from the feuding Montague and Capulet families.

tossups.p: This play opens with a 14-line sonnet spoken by a Chorus describing “two households, both alike in dignity.” Its heroine’s talkative old Nurse serves as a go-between, carrying secret messages to the man she has just married.
tossups.r: That marriage is performed in secret by a friendly friar. For 10 points, name this tragedy of two star-crossed young lovers, written by William Shakespeare, set in the feuding city of Verona.

tossups.p: A witty friend of this play’s hero mockingly nicknames a hotheaded swordsman, the cousin of the hero’s new wife, the “Prince of Cats.” That swordsman later kills the witty friend, Mercutio, who had delivered an earlier speech about the tiny fairy Queen Mab.
tossups.r: The hero kills the swordsman in revenge and is banished from Verona as punishment. For 10 points, name this Shakespeare tragedy about two star-crossed lovers from the feuding Montague and Capulet families.

Mercutio mockingly nicknames his rival swordsman the “Prince of Cats” shortly before their fatal duel
From her balcony, the heroine bids her admirer good night with the line “parting is such sweet sorrow”

trap.title: Verona or Manhattan?
trap.body: West Side Story borrows this play’s entire plot — two feuding groups, a secret romance, a tragic ending — but moves it to 1950s New York with rival gangs instead of noble families. Tony, Maria, the Jets, and the Sharks belong to the musical, not this play.
trap.fix: If the clue names Verona, the Montagues, or the Capulets, it’s this play. If it names the Jets, the Sharks, Tony, or Maria, it’s West Side Story instead.
trap.line: Real answer line: Romeo and Juliet (accept The Tragedy of Romeo and Juliet).
